content.text: prostaglandin inhibitors (eg, indomethacin) modestly ↓polyuria in nephrogenic DI, generally by no more than 10 to 25%.

Boxed: NSAIDs ↑ risk of serious CV thrombotic events, incl MI and stroke, which can be fatal; risk may occur early in tx and may ↑ w/ duration of use. Boxed: contraindicated in the setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. Boxed: NSAIDs ↑ risk of serious GI adverse events incl bleeding, ulceration, and perforation of the stomach or intestines, which can be fatal; can occur at any time and w/o warning symptoms; elderly pts and pts w/ prior peptic ulcer disease and/or GI bleeding at greater risk. CI: known hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylactic reactions and serious skin reactions) to indomethacin or any components of the drug product. CI: Hx of asthma, urticaria, or other allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs. Recent MI: avoid unless benefits expected to outweigh the risk of recurrent CV thrombotic events; if used, monitor for signs of cardiac ischemia. Minimize GI risk: lowest effective dosage for the shortest possible duration; ⍉ more than one NSAID at a time; ⍉ use in pts at higher risk unless benefits outweigh the ↑ bleeding risk; if a serious GI event is suspected, promptly evaluate and discontinue indomethacin until it is ruled out. ALT or AST three or more times ULN reported in ~1% of NSAID-treated pts in clinical trials. If signs/symptoms consistent w/ liver disease develop, or systemic manifestations occur (e.g., eosinophilia, rash), discontinue immediately and perform a clinical evaluation. Can cause new-onset or worsening hypertension; pts on ACE inhibitors, thiazide or loop diuretics may have impaired response. Correct volume status in dehydrated or hypovolemic pts b4 initiating; monitor renal function in renal or hepatic impairment, heart failure, dehydration, or hypovolemia. Limit NSAID use between about 20 to 30 wks in pregnancy (risk of oligohydramnios/fetal renal dysfunction); ⍉ use at about 30 wks gestation and later (also premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus). ↑ risk of bleeding events w/ coagulation disorders or concomitant warfarin, other anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents (e.g., aspirin), SSRIs, or SNRIs; monitor for signs of bleeding. OD Sx typically limited to lethargy, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, and epigastric pain, generally reversible w/ supportive care; GI bleeding has occurred; hypertension, acute renal failure, respiratory depression, and coma occurred but were rare. OD tx: symptomatic and supportive care; there are no specific antidotes; consider emesis and/or activated charcoal and/or osmotic cathartic in symptomatic pts within four hours of ingestion or w/ a large overdosage (5 to 10 times the recommended dosage).
